title: 2009 AMC 12B Problem 23
statement:
A region \(S\) in the complex plane is defined by \[ \scriptsize S = \{x + iy : -1 \le x \le 1,\ -1 \le y \le 1\}. \]

A complex number \(z = x + iy\) is chosen uniformly at random from \(S.\) What is the probability that \(\left(\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}i\right)z\) is also in \(S?\)

solutions.text:
Expanding, \(\left(\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}i\right)(x + iy)\) \(= \dfrac{3}{4}(x - y)\) \(+ \dfrac{3}{4}(x + y)i.\) Both parts lie in \([-1, 1]\) iff \(|x - y| \le \dfrac{4}{3}\) and \(|x + y| \le \dfrac{4}{3}.\)

Within the square \(S\) (area \(4\)) these fail only in four corner triangles. Near \((1, 1),\) the line \(x + y = \dfrac{4}{3}\) cuts off a right triangle with legs \(\dfrac{2}{3},\) area \(\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{2}{9}.\)

The four corners remove \(4 \cdot \dfrac{2}{9} = \dfrac{8}{9},\) leaving \(4 - \dfrac{8}{9} = \dfrac{28}{9}.\) The probability is \(\dfrac{\frac{28}{9}}{4} = \dfrac{7}{9}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Multiplying gives real part \(\tfrac{3}{4}(x - y)\) and imaginary part \(\tfrac{3}{4}(x + y)\); both must lie in \([-1, 1]\)
These conditions are \(|x - y| \le \tfrac{4}{3}\) and \(|x + y| \le \tfrac{4}{3}\); find the area of \(S\) satisfying them
